# DIN, HSTU, LONGER, SlimPer, and RankMixer: what interacts with what?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 73 topic entries / 5 representative comparisons

Before comparing ranking backbones, trace history-to-history, candidate-to-history, and field-to-field edges. DIN activates history by candidate; HSTU updates historical states across layers; LONGER merges tokens before a short query reads long KV; SlimPer repeatedly reads the user pool but propagates only a small knowledge base; RankMixer replaces heterogeneous field interactions. These mechanisms may occupy different stages in one pipeline. A single length variable or local leaderboard cannot rank them all.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Compare layer-to-layer state before FLOPs

HSTU updates the history window in every layer; LONGER continues on short query outputs after the first; SlimPer keeps original user tokens readable while propagating a small KB. They save different things. Eliminating full-length propagated state does not eliminate long-history reads, and eliminating softmax does not eliminate pairwise history interactions. DIN's target pooling and RankMixer's field mixing also do not fit one N²-versus-N table.

Sources: [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md) · [LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en.md) · [SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart](../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en.md) · [Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction](../../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en.md) · [RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2507.15551-rankmixer/README-en.md)

### A user-side label does not guarantee reuse across candidates

DIN pooling already reads the candidate. SlimPer's KB begins with item/cross information, so candidate B cannot reuse A's refined KB. HSTU M-FALCON and LONGER user KV reuse require a shared path that has not consumed target-dependent information. RankMixer often mixes candidates, sequence summaries, and fields late, so its final state is not inherently a reusable user cache. Trace dependencies rather than module names.

Sources: [Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction](../../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en.md) · [SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart](../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en.md) · [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md) · [LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en.md) · [RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2507.15551-rankmixer/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### LONGER and SlimPer both compress state. Why does compressing once and never reading the full history again describe only some paths? {#cross-which-history-remains-readable}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** LONGER's first short queries read long KV; later layers mostly work on the short output. SlimPer's small KB queries the user token pool at every layer, retaining access to original evidence. HSTU instead updates history within the window across layers. Ask what each layer can still access instead of calling all three short-sequence compression.

    **Illustrative example:** If an old gardening interaction was missed in layer one, SlimPer can query it again later. LONGER cannot reread it from the full history if the short sequence did not retain it.

    Sources: [LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en.md) · [SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart](../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en.md) · [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md)

### When scoring 100 candidates for one user, can DIN interests, SlimPer KBs, and HSTU historical KV all be cached once? {#cross-candidate-dependent-cache}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DIN interests and SlimPer's final KB depend on the candidate. Only base encodings that have not read the target are shareable. Under M-FALCON, HSTU reuses candidate-independent historical KV, but each target still needs its own query and output. A cache requires fixed dependencies, not just the same user.

    **Illustrative example:** A cat-food candidate makes the KB focus on cat ownership. A gardening-tool candidate should attend to flower growing. Reusing the cat-food KB would mistake one target-conditioned state for a general user state.

    Sources: [Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction](../../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en.md) · [SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart](../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en.md) · [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md)

### If RankMixer does not use attention for interactions, why can it coexist with LONGER or HSTU? {#cross-field-mixing-not-history-replacement}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** RankMixer handles interactions across heterogeneous field tokens. LONGER and HSTU focus on behavioral history. A history module can produce a summary or state as input fields for TokenMix and PFFN. Field count T and history length N are different variables, so replacing field attention does not determine full-model cost or long-history capability.

    **Illustrative example:** A history module emits recent and long-term interests. Alongside price, device, and candidate category, these make five field tokens. Late TokenMix does not replace upstream history retrieval and encoding.

    Sources: [RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2507.15551-rankmixer/README-en.md) · [LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en.md) · [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md)
